title: Crash when quitting due to dangling `CSharpScript` reference
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in `v4.7.beta4.mono.official [dff2b9bb6]`
- Reproducible in `v4.6.1` (I don't have the build hash anymore)

### System information

macOS Sequoia 15.6.1

### Issue description

I spent a significant amount of time investigating this and trying to create a minimal repro, but no matter how much I tried, I could only repro this with my closed-source game. 😢 Even then, the repro only happens:

- After waiting >5 seconds from launching my game to quitting it
- About half the time I made an attempt
- After invoking `StartDialogue` in [the Yarn Spinner library](https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Godot)

In short, the problem was that quitting my game via `GetTree().Quit();` would sometimes crash with the following `--verbose` log:

<details><summary>Crash log</summary>

```
Quitting the game
Unloading: Disposing tracked instances...
Unloading: Finished disposing tracked instances.
XR: Clearing primary interface
XR: Removed interface "Native mobile"
XR: Removed interface "OpenXR"

================================================================
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.7.beta4.mono.official (dff2b9bb66a01d8c1a207531b0752405c7399124)
Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug on: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues
Load address: 10440c000

Freeing Default Tex_Blit Shader
MultiUmaBuffer 'RENDER_LIST_OPAQUE' used a total of 0 buffers. A large number may indicate a waste of VRAM and can be brought down by tweaking MAX_EXTRA_BUFFERS for this buffer.
MultiUmaBuffer 'RENDER_LIST_MOTION' used a total of 0 buffers. A large number may indicate a waste of VRAM and can be brought down by tweaking MAX_EXTRA_BUFFERS for this buffer.
MultiUmaBuffer 'RENDER_LIST_ALPHA' used a total of 0 buffers. A large number may indicate a waste of VRAM and can be brought down by tweaking MAX_EXTRA_BUFFERS for this buffer.
MultiUmaBuffer 'RENDER_LIST_SECONDARY' used a total of 0 buffers. A large number may indicate a waste of VRAM and can be brought down by tweaking MAX_EXTRA_BUFFERS for this buffer.
MultiUmaBuffer 'CANVAS_INSTANCE_DATA' used a total of 3 buffers. A large number may indicate a waste of VRAM and can be brought down by tweaking MAX_EXTRA_BUFFERS for this buffer.
Accessibility: window 0 adapter destroyed.
WARNING: 1 ObjectDB instance was leaked at exit (run with `--verbose` for details).
   at: cleanup (core/object/object.cpp:2535)
Leaked instance: CSharpScript:9223372155201262094 - Reference count: 0
Hint: Leaked instances typically happen when nodes are removed from the scene tree (with `remove_child()`) but not freed (with `free()` or `queue_free()`).
ERROR: 1 resources still in use at exit.
   at: clear (core/io/resource.cpp:817)
Resource still in use: res://addons/YarnSpinner-Godot/Runtime/Views/ActionMarkupHandler.cs (CSharpScript)
Orphan StringName: MusicSlider (static: 0, total: 1)
[...omitted other orphans for brevity...]
StringName: 342 unclaimed string names at exit.
```
</details>

Note: no backtrace actually printed out, so I dove into `lldb` with an unoptimized dev build of Godot. It broke in here:

```
* thread #1, queue = 'com.apple.main-thread', stop reason = EXC_BREAKPOINT (code=1, subcode=0x101aee14c)
    frame #0: 0x0000000101aee14c godot.macos.editor.dev.arm64.mono`SelfList<CSharpScript>::List::~List(this=0x000000011fcfe1c0) at self_list.h:135:4
   132
   133 			_FORCE_INLINE_ ~List() {
   134 				// A self list must be empty on destruction.
-> 135 				DEV_ASSERT(_first == nullptr);
   136 			}
   137 		};
   138
```

Here's where I don't claim to understand everything, so I'll include any relevant details I could piece together:

- Most importantly, calling this code before quitting brings the repro rate to 0 out of 30 attempts (i.e. this is the workaround I plan to use to stop my game from crashing at exit):

```cs
GC.Collect();
GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers();
GC.Collect();
```
- The `CSharpScript` still in use is [`ActionMarkupHandler.cs`](https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Godot/blob/008db59b96e8fb28a74bd1ca7176688963cf09ac/addons/YarnSpinner-Godot/Runtime/Views/ActionMarkupHandler.cs).
   - It's `abstract`, and since I've run into [an issue using `abstract` Godot nodes](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75230) before, I tried making it concrete. It didn't seem to impact the repro.
   - I believe the _actual_ problem comes from [this `Array<ActionMarkupHandler>`](https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Godot/blob/008db59b96e8fb28a74bd1ca7176688963cf09ac/addons/YarnSpinner-Godot/Runtime/Async/LinePresenter.cs#L185) in Yarn Spinner, which eventually gets copied into a `List` [here](https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Godot/blob/008db59b96e8fb28a74bd1ca7176688963cf09ac/addons/YarnSpinner-Godot/Runtime/Async/LinePresenter.cs#L218).
   - Despite that Yarn Spinner is non-Godot code, I don't think Godot itself should crash when quitting, which is why I'm filing the bug in this repo.
- I investigated this while streaming, and while I don't recommend anyone actually watch 8 hours' worth of videos, they _are_ available: [part 1](https://youtu.be/SKSdb08_KkA?t=8239), [part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Ymi4isbeIA), [part 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lLH46v9sp3k).
